newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen hovering around lower levels.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen hovering around lower levels.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse was expected to hover around the lower levels reached on Tuesday for the rest of the week after a weaker dollar and losses on Bunds weighed on the market.
"We should go sideways or nervously move back and forth as long we see no big move on Wall Street," said one dealer.
The IBIS DAX, measuring all-day electronic dealings in the DAX index of 30 top German shares, was down 32.77 at 2,808.39 points by 1521 GMT, below the bourse close of 2,815.13.
The IBIS DAX came off lows under the crucial 2,800 point mark as Wall Street reversed early losses and traded up.

Dealers said the 2,800 point mark should hold this week and saw the DAX index trading in a range between 2,800 and 2,825 points. "We've had a terrific year and we don't want to go and ruin that in the last two weeks of the year," said one dealer.
The IBIS DAX had slipped down to 2,795.32 points, tracking Bunds lower after stronger-than-expected U.S. November housing starts at 1.514 million against an expected 1.390 million.
Meanwhile the German market was waiting for the outcome of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday afternoon, although the Fed was widely seen keeping interest rates steady.
Shares in export-oriented chemicals companies like Hoechst AG and BASF AG lost ground as the dollar slipped below 1.55 marks, weighing on other exporting stocks.

Meanwhile, Commerzbank was one of the few large stocks to buck the downward trend, up 28 pfennigs at 38.38 marks in lat IBIS dealings on a resurgence of takeover speculation in the banking sector, although the bank said it had no comment to make on such rumours.
Deutsche Lufthansa was also firmer, up 35 pfennigs at 20.80 marks, with dealers saying the stock was poised to test technical resistance at 21 marks.
